item.text: {"A":"Research an exact sparse-obstacle candidate for low M: deduplicate blocked coordinates, sort them in a valid dependency order, and use binomial path counts with inclusion-exclusion to compute paths avoiding earlier obstacles, then evaluate the destination. Precompute factorials and inverse factorials modulo 1000000007 (the largest needed factorial index is below the modulus). Handle blocked start or destination and N=1 explicitly. The pairwise work can be O(M^2), so do not assume the stated M bound makes M small: include a cost-based switch or exact fallback for larger M. Check duplicate obstacles and coordinate ordering against the baseline semantics.","B":"Optimize the dense row-DP as an independently correct, linear-memory candidate. Replace the N-by-N blocked grid with O(N+M) storage, such as per-row sorted blocked columns; use two O(N) DP rows and swap them instead of copying a row each iteration. Preserve the row recurrence, modular arithmetic, and output exactly. Focus on memory and practical dense-case performance; the O(N^2) traversal remains. Measure arithmetic or representation changes rather than assuming they help, and retain a correct path for all valid inputs.","C":"Investigate an exact four-core parallel implementation of the dense DP. Within each row, blocked cells reset the recurrence; each open run is an inclusive prefix sum of the previous row's values. Explore a parallel segmented scan with correct handling of runs crossing chunk boundaries, while keeping row dependencies sequential. Benchmark parallel overhead, especially on small cases, and use no more than the available four CPU cores. Do not rely on GPU or on changing the compiler or evaluation setup.","G":"Evaluate A, B, and C candidates standalone for correctness and runtime under the unchanged evaluation setup before integrating anything. Consider a measured hybrid such as sparse combinatorial handling for low M and a linear-memory DP fallback, but derive dispatch from general cost/performance evidence, not particular test inputs. Re-test the integrated program: gains may not add, and a combination can be slower than its components. Keep the fastest correct option, preserve behavior for every valid input, and verify blocked endpoints, duplicates, modular results, and output formatting.","analysis":"The supplied source is the grid-path problem (Problem D). Its baseline is correct on 4 cases and measured at a mean of 0.079210793 seconds (individual times about 0.07918–0.07923 seconds), with score 0.5; no alternative measurements are available, so no speedup is established. The source allocates an N-by-N blocked grid and performs O(N^2) DP work, while the statement permits N below 200000 and only gives an upper bound on M that does not guarantee M is small enough for an O(M^2) method. The main research directions are therefore exact sparse handling with a safe fallback, reducing dense-path memory, and testing whether intra-row parallelism pays on the ARM64 four-core, no-GPU target."}
